title: AI-Assisted Data Quality and Lineage System
summary: Profiling, rule checks, and drift detection across datasets, with field-level lineage and AI-written explanations that a data steward approves before any correction runs.
primaryMessage: I use AI to assist governed data operations while keeping human control over consequential changes.

executive.problem: Bad data reaches reports and models because checks are scattered, failures are hard to interpret, and nobody can quickly see which downstream tables a broken field affects.
executive.approach: One service profiles data, runs rules and drift checks, traces lineage down to the field, and uses a language model to explain each failure and propose a fix that a steward reviews.
executive.impact: Stewards see what broke, why, and what it touches in one place, and every correction has an approver and an audit record.
executive.whyItMatters: Shows how to apply AI inside governed data operations: the model drafts explanations and proposals, people approve changes, and the system keeps the record.

problem: Data teams find quality issues late, often from a business user. Rule failures arrive as cryptic messages, lineage lives in people's heads, and fixes are applied by hand without a record of who approved them. Regulated environments need both speed and an audit trail.
users: Data stewards who own quality for a domain
Analysts and model owners who consume the data

constraints.detail: No automated change to production data without a named approver.
Explanations are generated from profiles and samples with sensitive fields masked.
Checks must run on schedule and on pipeline completion without blocking ingestion.
Findings, proposals, approvals, and applied changes are stored immutably.

zones.label: Human approval boundary: nothing crosses into production without a steward

architectureNotes: The model never writes to data stores. It produces an explanation and a proposed change object; only the change runner applies approved proposals.
Lineage is captured from pipeline run events so impact analysis reflects what actually ran.
Explanations receive profiles, rule definitions, and masked samples, never raw sensitive values.

aiTechnique.choice: Statistical and rule-based detection, with a language model used only for explanation and fix drafting.
aiTechnique.rationale: Detection must be deterministic and testable, so it uses rules, schema checks, and statistical drift tests. The language model adds value where people struggle: turning a failure plus lineage into a readable explanation and a candidate fix.

rejected.reason: Non-deterministic, costly at scale, and hard to test; statistics do this job better.
Unacceptable in governed environments; a wrong fix silently corrupts downstream data.

implementation.detail: Column statistics, null and uniqueness rates, declarative rules, and schema contracts per dataset.
Population stability and distribution tests against a rolling reference window; volume anomalies per run.
OpenLineage-compatible events stored as a dataset and field graph for upstream and downstream traversal.
FastAPI service for findings, proposals, and approvals; review queue for stewards.
Append-only table recording finding, proposal, approver, decision, and applied change.
Routing by dataset owner with severity and affected downstream assets.
Seeded datasets with injected defects; tests assert each defect is detected and traced.

datasets: Synthetic datasets with injected defects: nulls, duplicates, type changes, range violations, distribution shifts
Lineage fixtures with known upstream and downstream paths
baselines: Explanations from rule messages alone, without an LLM

metrics.name: Defect detection recall
metrics.target: Share of injected defects detected, by defect type
metrics.method: Compare findings to the injection manifest

metrics.name: False alert rate
metrics.target: Alerts on clean batches per 100 runs
metrics.method: Count findings on batches with no injected defects

metrics.name: Explanation accuracy
metrics.target: Steward rating of explanation correctness and usefulness
metrics.method: Blind steward review with a fixed rubric

regression: Every injected defect type must be detected on each CI run
Lineage traversal tests on fixed graphs
failureAnalysis: Missed defects grouped by type and threshold
Explanations rated wrong are reviewed for missing context versus model error

humanControl.detail: Every proposed correction waits for a named steward's decision.
Findings, proposals, decisions, and applied changes are immutable and queryable.
Sensitive fields are masked before any text reaches the model.
High-severity findings affecting many downstream assets notify owners directly.

expected: Detection of all injected defect types in the fixture set
Shorter steward triage time with explanations and lineage than with raw rule messages

limitations: Synthetic defects do not cover every real-world failure pattern.
Lineage is only as complete as the pipelines that emit events.
Explanation quality has not been measured with real stewards.
Triage-time improvement is a hypothesis until a timed study is run.

setup: docker compose exec api python -m seed --with-defects
docker compose exec api pytest tests/
reproduction.testData: Synthetic tables generated by the seed script with a manifest of injected defects.
reproduction.credentials: Local steward and engineer demo accounts defined in .env.example.
reproduction.expectedOutput: Findings for each injected defect, lineage impact lists, and pending proposals in the review queue.
